nota: Each block becomes one audio file. Sentences are separated by [long pause]; tools/audio-split.py cuts the file at those pauses and the app plays each sentence on its own, at the right time. The text of each sentence is exactly what the screen shows.

masculina.sugestao: Jerry B. - Calm Meditation | Soothing & Relaxing Voice

frases: This is the For Now voice. One sentence at a time, no rush.
Feel where your feet meet the floor.
Pick one object in front of you.
Notice a color or a detail on it.
Now notice a sound nearby.
You can just stay with that for a moment.
That's okay. Come back to what's around you.
Touch something near you and notice its texture.
Notice if it's cool or warm, smooth or rough.
Now find three things of the same color.

blocos.nome: Breathe slowly, listen to a sound, stay, one more moment
frases: Let the air come in however it comes.
Let it out slowly, no rush.
No need to fill your chest or hold your breath.
Just let the out-breath be a little slower.
Keep going like this, at your own pace.
Choose a sound and stay with it for a moment.
When you notice you've started talking with a thought, you can come back to the sound.
No need to empty your mind. Just come back, as many times as it takes.
You can just stay with the sound.
I'll be quiet now. Stay with the sound.
Stay a little longer. Nothing to do.
If it's comfortable, gently close your hands.
Now let go. Notice the difference.
Lift your shoulders a little, without forcing.
And let them drop. Let your shoulders rest.
If any part hurts, you can just let go, without squeezing.
Gently scrunch your forehead and eyes.
Let your face go: forehead, eyes, jaw.
Press your feet gently into the floor.
And let your legs go.
Now let your body be heavy where it's resting.
Nothing else to do. Stay as long as you like.
Let your body sink into the mattress.
Let your shoulders go.
Let your hands be heavy.
No need to fall asleep now. Resting counts.
If thoughts come, let them pass like noise outside.
I'll be quiet now.
Your alarm is set.
Feel the pillow supporting you.
You can rest now. If you don't fall asleep, that's fine: resting counts.
Your alarm is in the phone's Clock.
This rest has no alarm.
You can rest now.
Box breathing. Breathe in, hold, breathe out and pause, all for the same time. Follow the circle.
Four, seven, eight breathing. Breathe in counting to four, hold to seven and let it out slowly to eight.
Coherent breathing. Breathe in and out at the same pace, slowly, like a wave.
Long exhale. Let the breath out last longer than the breath in.
Double sigh. Breathe in through your nose, take in a little more, and let it all out very slowly through your mouth.
Breathing at your own timing. Follow the circle.
If it feels uncomfortable, go back to breathing normally. You can shorten the times.
You can go back to breathing at your own pace.
Notice how your body feels now.
Breathe in through your nose.
Breathe in.
A little more air.
Hold the air.
Hold.
Let the air out slowly.
Breathe out.
And let it all out, slowly.
Pause.
Lie down in the way that is most comfortable for you.
Put the phone aside. You do not need to look at the screen.
Let the air out slowly, a little longer than usual.
Once more. Let the breath out be slow.
Now bring your attention to your feet.
Let your feet be heavy, sinking into the mattress.
Move up to your legs. Let your legs be loose.
Your hips and belly can rest too.
Notice your chest rising and falling, without controlling anything.
Now your hands. Let your hands be heavy and warm.
Your arms, up to your shoulders. Let your shoulders drop.
Your neck can rest on the pillow.
Release your jaw, your tongue, your forehead and your eyes.
If thoughts come, let them pass, like clouds.
You do not need to try to sleep. Resting already counts.
Imagine a peaceful place where you like to be.
Notice the colors, the sounds and the temperature of that place.
Let your body get heavier and heavier.
I will be quiet now. The music goes on for a while.
Good night.
